classes.name: Object
classes.doc: The root of everything with identity. Has metadata, has a rationale, can be asked what it is.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Opaque identity. A string or opaque handle — NEVER a u64, because TS integers alias past 2^53.

fields.name: type_path
fields.doc: The mount-pointed class path this object was instantiated from.

fields.name: rationale
fields.doc: Why the core did what it did with this object. Core-written.

methods.name: is_a
methods.doc: Class-membership test against a picked class path.

methods.name: equals
methods.doc: Identity comparison. Never a float comparison.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: Short display form.

methods.name: explain
methods.doc: Prose a developer reads in the trace.

methods.name: meta
methods.doc: Read one metadata value.

methods.doc: Write one metadata value. The CV_ prefix is reserved for the core and rejected here.

methods.name: has_meta
methods.doc: Is this key set?

methods.name: remove_meta

methods.name: _configure
methods.doc: Setup phase 1. Own configuration only; other content may not exist yet.

methods.name: _resolve
methods.doc: Setup phase 2. Every registered content class now exists and may be referenced.

classes.name: Actor
classes.doc: Something placeable in a world. The only thing the core places, and the sole point of contact between content and generation.

fields.name: components
fields.doc: Attached components, in attach order — which is the order every aggregating hook walks.

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: The actor this one is mounted on, if any.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc: Local transform relative to the parent.

fields.name: skip_policy
fields.doc: Whether alternative routes past this actor's gate are tolerated, reported, or actively forbidden. Inert unless gate() is non-trivial.

fields.name: discoverability
fields.doc: The declared likelihood a player finds this gate's solution unprompted. Declared because it is not derivable; above the threshold the solver treats the gate as open, conservatively, and names it in the trace.

methods.name: component
methods.doc: First attached component of that kind.

methods.name: components_of
methods.doc: Every attached component of that kind.

methods.name: add_component
methods.doc: Attach a component.

methods.name: remove_component
methods.doc: Detach a component.

methods.name: attach_to
methods.doc: Mount this actor onto another at a named socket.

methods.name: world_transform
methods.doc: Absolute transform. Walks the parent chain, so it is not free.

methods.name: pivot
methods.doc: The point this actor rotates and mounts about.

methods.name: bounds
methods.doc: Axis-aligned extent.

methods.name: footprint
methods.doc: The space this reserves during skeleton layout.

methods.name: clearance
methods.doc: Space that must stay empty around this actor. Called per candidate position, so it must stay cheap.

methods.name: collision
methods.doc: What this actor physically blocks.

methods.name: mount_faces
methods.doc: Which faces this may be mounted against. Floor, wall or ceiling is what distinguishes a chest from a sconce from a chandelier.

methods.name: up_axis
methods.doc: Which direction is up for this actor.

methods.name: yaw_snap
methods.doc: Rotational quantisation about the up axis. 0 = free, 4 = 90 degrees.

methods.name: allow_pitch
methods.doc: May the solver tilt this out of the up axis?

methods.name: allow_roll
methods.doc: May the solver roll this about its forward axis?

methods.name: scalable
methods.doc: Permitted uniform scale range. A lever a fixed-template system cannot have; convexity is affine-invariant, so the collision cache survives it.

methods.name: uniform_scale_only
methods.doc: Forbid non-uniform scaling.

methods.name: embed_depth
methods.doc: How far this may sink into the surface it mounts on.

methods.name: constraints
methods.doc: Hard placement constraints. A door names its own unlock here, which is where key-to-lock distance is written.

methods.name: preferences
methods.doc: Soft placement biases. Relaxable, and reported when relaxed.

methods.name: eligible_roles
methods.doc: Which roles this actor may be assigned. Role is an output; this only narrows the candidate set.

methods.name: schedule
methods.doc: Ordering rules relative to other content.

methods.name: quota
methods.doc: How many of this may exist, per scope.

methods.name: weight
methods.doc: Selection bias among eligible candidates.

methods.name: repulsion
methods.doc: How strongly instances of this push away from each other. A pressure, never an obligation.

methods.name: enables
methods.doc: What can be done here.
methods.default: aggregate enabled components in attach order

methods.name: requires
methods.doc: What must exist near me for my mechanic to work. This is the hook that makes the generator place enabling content.
methods.default: aggregate enabled components in attach order

methods.name: forbids
methods.doc: What must NOT be near me. The negative half of an obligation.
methods.default: aggregate enabled components in attach order

methods.name: judge
methods.doc: Is this proposal good, and how wrong is it? The magnitude is the point: a boolean turns the placement search into a reroll.

methods.name: gate
methods.doc: What the occupant must hold to pass.

methods.name: harm
methods.doc: Is this dangerous, how much, and is it avoidable?

methods.name: grants
methods.doc: Unlocks the occupant keeps after reaching this. ROWS of an UnlockTableResource, never classes — the lattice is over identities and a row id already is one. An unlock carries NO behaviour: every mechanical consequence belongs to a Component.
methods.default: aggregate enabled components in attach order

methods.name: quantity

methods.name: replenishes
methods.doc: Whether and how this comes back.

classes.name: Component
classes.doc: An attachable behaviour with its own transform. The seven hooks have the same signatures as Actor, and this is where a mechanic is written.

fields.name: owner
fields.doc: The actor this is attached to.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Disabled components are skipped by every aggregating hook.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc: Local transform relative to the owner.

methods.name: world_transform
methods.doc: Absolute transform. Walks the parent chain, so it is not free.

methods.name: on_attached
methods.doc: Event: attached to an actor.

methods.name: on_detached
methods.doc: Event: detached from an actor.

methods.name: validate

methods.name: replenishes

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: Visible is not the same as collidable.

classes.doc: A parametric shape. Collision is computed analytically from its parameters, never from tessellation.

fields.name: surface
fields.doc: The Surface class this shape presents.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: Visible is not the same as collidable.

methods.name: collision
methods.doc: The analytically derived collision body.

classes.name: MountComponent
classes.doc: An attachment socket. What may mount here is a tag query, not a hand-maintained class list.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: A label for a developer reading the viewport. Deliberately not a lookup key.

fields.name: faces
fields.doc: Which faces of the mounted thing may meet this socket.

fields.name: clearance
fields.doc: Space that must stay empty around whatever mounts here.

methods.name: admits
methods.doc: Whether a specific candidate may mount, beyond the tag query.

classes.name: TraversalComponent
classes.doc: Turns a spatial delta into a directed graph edge. The thing that makes a staircase a route rather than scenery.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Horizontal distance this move covers.

methods.name: rise
methods.doc: Vertical delta this move covers. Negative is downward.

methods.name: direction
methods.doc: Permitted directions as a cone, so 'up, level or diagonally up, never down' is expressible.

methods.name: admits
methods.doc: What the occupant must hold to make this move, IN THIS DIRECTION — so one edge can be open one way and gated the other.

methods.name: cost
methods.doc: What traversing this spends against a route budget.

methods.name: approach
methods.doc: What the occupant needs at the near end before the move is possible.

classes.name: CheckpointComponent
classes.doc: A place that returns the world to a known-good state. P15's second satisfaction route, and what lets the solver take an attractive one-way transition instead of refusing every irreversible edge.

fields.name: restores
fields.doc: Which CLASSES OF PLACED CONTENT respawn here -- consumables, destructibles, enemies. NOT unlocks: an unlock is monotone and can never be lost, so restoring one has no meaning.

fields.name: restores_occupant
fields.doc: Whether the occupant also returns here — which is what makes this a respawn point as well.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: How far this checkpoint's effect reaches.

classes.name: FastTravelComponent
classes.doc: A node in a travel network. Not cosmetic: a network collapses traversal cost across the whole World, and difficulty here IS slack spent against a budget.

fields.name: network
fields.doc: Nodes sharing a network name connect to each other.

fields.name: cost
fields.doc: What one hop spends — in the same currency as the routes it competes with.

fields.name: unlocked_by
fields.doc: What the occupant must hold before this node joins its network.

classes.name: StateSetterComponent
classes.doc: Writes a world-state variable. The authoring surface for the non-monotone axis.

fields.name: variable
fields.doc: Which declared state variable this writes.

fields.name: while_occupied_by
fields.doc: If set, the value holds only WHILE something carrying this component is present — which is what makes dwell an ordinary reading rather than a trigger kind.

classes.name: BlocksTraversalComponent
classes.doc: Place me on an edge of this kind, and close it. Without this a barrier can only be authored as geometry, which violates gate-never-delete by construction.

fields.name: matching
fields.doc: Which kind of traversal edge this may be placed on.

fields.name: route
fields.doc: The route this blocker obliges or forbids.

classes.name: Surface
classes.doc: What a piece of geometry means to a mechanic. Answers who may be here and what works here.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Why an eligible-surface list is a TagQuery rather than a hand-maintained class list. The editor must show these on selected geometry.

methods.name: supports
methods.doc: Can something BE here? A state you are in, evaluated per occupant and per sphere.

methods.name: affords
methods.doc: Does an ACTION work here? Covers transit THROUGH as well as action UPON, which is how one pane of glass blocks ballistics and walking while passing a laser and a sightline.

methods.name: friction
methods.doc: Traversal resistance.

methods.name: harm
methods.doc: Is standing here dangerous?

methods.name: admits_mount
methods.doc: May something mount against this surface?

classes.name: Rule
classes.doc: Sealed on purpose: the solver walks this tree as the analysable half of a gate, so a developer-defined rule would make the dependency walk impossible.

methods.name: is_open
methods.doc: Does this rule currently hold?

methods.name: referenced
methods.doc: Every unlock this rule mentions. The solver's dependency walk, and what lets requires() plant a source.

methods.name: explain
methods.doc: Prose for a lock badge and the trace.

classes.name: AlwaysRule
classes.doc: Trivially satisfied. The identity of AllOfRule.

classes.name: NeverRule
classes.doc: Never satisfied. The identity of AnyOfRule. On a sole route this is an authoring error and is reported with the numbers, not silently accepted.

classes.name: HoldsRule
classes.doc: The occupant holds this unlock, or anything that supersedes it.

fields.name: unlock
fields.doc: The unlock required. Satisfied by this row, or by any held unlock whose supersedes closure contains it.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many. Quantity lives here, not in a number of instances.

classes.name: HasComponentRule
classes.doc: The occupant holds something CARRYING a matching component. A DIFFERENT question from HoldsRule: this asks about the things held, that asks about the lattice.

classes.name: AllOfRule
classes.doc: Every child holds.

classes.name: AnyOfRule
classes.doc: At least one child holds. This is what proves genuine alternate routes rather than one route the solver happened to pick.

classes.name: NegateRule
classes.doc: The inner rule does NOT hold. Non-monotonic, so it is accepted and reported rather than refused.

classes.name: NearbyRule
classes.doc: Something matching is accessible within range of this gate. The contextual half: a gate may depend on the WORLD rather than only the occupant, and because the dependency walk sees it, requires() can plant the source.

fields.name: within
fields.doc: How near, in whatever currency the budget names.

classes.name: Verdict
classes.doc: What judge() returns. A boolean would tell the solver nothing and turn the placement search into a reroll.

classes.name: AcceptedVerdict
classes.doc: It fits. The slack says how comfortably, which feeds difficulty.

classes.name: OverBudgetVerdict
classes.doc: Too far. Move the target closer by roughly this much — a direction the solver can act on.

fields.name: against
fields.doc: Which budget it was measured against. 'Over budget by 6.2' leaves a developer guessing; 'over budget by 6.2 against grapple reach' names the lever to pull. Null only where the comparison was against a bare number.

classes.name: BlockedVerdict
classes.doc: Something is in the way. Remove or reposition that, or route around it.

classes.name: UnsuitableVerdict
classes.doc: Wrong kind of thing. Do not retry this candidate.

classes.name: Interaction
classes.doc: Something an occupant attempts. Subclassed by what relocates, which is what lets one surface answer four mechanics differently.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: How far this reaches. NOT named 'reach' — Reach is a scope.

fields.name: line_of_sight
fields.doc: Whether an unobstructed line is required.

fields.name: from_standing
fields.doc: Whether the occupant must be supported to attempt this.

methods.name: consumes
methods.doc: What performing this spends. What consumes a resource is the consumer, not the consumable.

methods.name: gate
methods.doc: What the occupant must hold to perform this. Deliberately the same name and meaning as Actor.gate, and deliberately NOT 'requires', which on an Actor means something unrelated.

methods.name: explain
methods.doc: Prose for the trace.

classes.name: Movement
classes.doc: THE PLAYER relocates, so this is a directed graph edge.

classes.name: Displace
classes.doc: AN OBJECT relocates, not the player. Push, carry and throw are authored subclasses of this.

classes.name: RemoteUse
classes.doc: NOTHING relocates — it acts at range. Sightlines, beams and ballistics are authored subclasses, which is how transit through a surface is expressed without a core enum.

methods.name: bounds

methods.name: volume

methods.name: is_convex

methods.name: closest_point

methods.name: decompose
methods.doc: Convex decomposition.

methods.name: sdf

classes.name: CubeShape

fields.name: center_post

classes.name: CompositeShape
classes.doc: A boolean combination of solid shapes.

classes.name: DiscShape

classes.name: EllipseShape
classes.doc: A flat ellipse.

methods.doc: The disjoint pieces.

classes.name: Resource

classes.name: UnlockTableResource
classes.doc: The project's progression vocabulary -- named rows, each one atom of the lattice. JSON, not the block notation, because it has no nodes to notate. A project may hold any number of these files anywhere under /Content; THE FILE IS THE UNIT OF SHARING, so copying it carries the vocabulary with it.

fields.name: rows
fields.doc: The row names, in file order.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: One row by display name. Convenience for authoring; by_id is the identity lookup.

methods.name: by_id
methods.doc: One row by its stable id. IDENTITY IS THE ID, never the name -- renaming a row must rewrite zero references.

classes.name: CurveTableResource
classes.doc: One or more NAMED CURVES over one NAMED DOMAIN AXIS. One resource type where UE has four: a vector curve is three rows, a colour curve is four. JSON, not the block notation, because it has no nodes to notate.

fields.name: domain
fields.doc: The axis rows are read over. Bound BY NAME to whichever ProgressionAxis carries it.

fields.name: y_label
fields.doc: Editor-only, so the vertical axis has a name.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: One row as a Curve struct.

methods.name: sample
methods.doc: Read a row at a domain value.

classes.name: ProgressionAxis
classes.doc: Supplies the x a curve row is sampled at. Built-ins cover depth, space count, unlock count and sphere; a developer subclasses it for anything else, which is the only way to say 'complexity gains weight each time a boss is placed'.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What a CurveTable's domain matches against.

methods.name: value
methods.doc: The current position along this axis. No default — a subclass must answer.

classes.name: Depth
classes.doc: Reach index divided by Reach count.

classes.name: SpaceCount
classes.doc: How many Spaces exist so far.

classes.name: UnlockCount
classes.doc: How many progression unlocks are held.

classes.name: Sphere
classes.doc: The current accessibility sphere.

classes.name: Route
classes.doc: A REQUIRED OR FORBIDDEN path with a budget, an occupant and predicates. The sign is in the primitive: a Span DECLARES a range, a Route OBLIGES one.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Origin. Null means unbound and resolved by the solver.

fields.name: occupant
fields.doc: Who traverses. Null means the player.

fields.name: party
fields.doc: Every listed occupant must traverse — an escort, not a simultaneous hold.

fields.name: line_of_sight
fields.doc: Whether an unobstructed line is obliged. An OBLIGATION, not an observation — which is what makes L4 keep it.

fields.name: from_standing
fields.doc: Whether the origin must be supported.

fields.name: forbidden
fields.doc: Content this route must not pass. The negative half.

classes.name: Budget
classes.doc: A NAMED limit — a row of the project's BudgetBook, referenced rather than copied. 'Carry range' is a concept a project tunes, not a number retyped at each of the five sites that mention it.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What a developer called it. Surfaces in the verdict, which is how a rejection says WHICH limit was missed.

fields.name: cost
fields.doc: The kind and the limit. Retuning this is the one edit that moves every site naming this budget.

methods.name: remaining
methods.doc: Unspent amount.

methods.name: spend
methods.doc: Consume from the budget. The argument is always a DISTANCE, whatever the budget measures — a caller that had to know whether to pass metres or seconds would re-derive the conversion at every call site and one of them would get it wrong.

methods.name: judge
methods.doc: Judge a distance against what is left, naming this budget in the verdict.

classes.name: BudgetBook
classes.doc: The project's named budgets — the one place 'carry range' is a number. NOTHING spends against a row here: open() hands out a working copy, because spending against the shared row would make two unrelated routes drain each other and the symptom would point nowhere near the cause.

methods.name: declare
methods.doc: Register a named budget.

methods.name: retune
methods.doc: Change what it costs. Every site naming it moves at once, which is the point; a site that inlined the number does not, which is also the point.

methods.name: by_name
methods.doc: Look one up by the name a developer typed.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: A working copy to spend against. Null for a reference the book does not hold — a dangling budget is a load-time diagnostic, never a default limit quietly standing in.

classes.name: DistanceCost
classes.doc: Metres.

classes.name: TimeCost
classes.doc: Seconds. Every TimeCost is a distance divided by player_profile.speed, which is why that setting is not optional.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: World units per second. Without it there is no way to turn seconds into a reachable distance.

classes.name: PoolCost
classes.doc: Draw against a named resource pool at a rate. How a soft gate is a magnitude rather than a rule — the solver can trade it off instead of treating it as impassable.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: How much of the pool may be drawn.

classes.name: NamedBudget
classes.doc: A row of the project's BudgetBook — retune it in one place and every site naming it moves.

classes.name: InlineBudget
classes.doc: A cost authored at this site. Right for a one-off; a magic number if it repeats — and because inline and named are told apart, a tool can notice when it has.

classes.name: Path
classes.doc: A realised route. What a Route becomes once the generator has produced it — and the reason there is no spline resource.

methods.name: steps
methods.doc: The ordered steps.

methods.name: length
methods.doc: Total distance.

methods.name: rise
methods.doc: Net vertical change.

methods.name: origin
methods.doc: Start point.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: End point.

classes.name: PathStep
classes.doc: One leg of a path.

methods.name: position
methods.doc: Where this leg starts.

methods.name: length
methods.doc: Leg distance.

methods.name: surface
methods.doc: What is underfoot.

methods.name: floor
methods.doc: Which Floor this leg is on.

methods.name: via
methods.doc: What made this leg possible.

classes.name: PlacementNeed
classes.doc: What requires() returns. The channel that makes the generator place enabling content.

classes.name: NeedsActor
classes.doc: Something carrying this component must exist, accessible by this route.

fields.name: having
fields.doc: The component the needed actor must carry. A CLASS reference — nothing is constructed.

classes.name: NeedsClearance
classes.doc: This volume must stay empty.

classes.name: BlocksTraversal
classes.doc: Place me ON an edge of this kind and close it.

classes.name: Constraint
classes.doc: A hard placement rule. Constraints express what CONTENT can state; dials express what only the generator can decide.

classes.name: AloneInScope
classes.doc: No sibling of this kind in the same scope.

classes.name: MinDistanceFrom
classes.doc: At least this far from a named kind. A door writes key-to-lock distance here, because the door names its own unlock and the key does not know its lock.

classes.name: MaxDistanceFrom
classes.doc: At most this far from a named kind.

classes.name: MountedOn
classes.doc: Must be mounted on a matching socket.

classes.name: WithinScope
classes.doc: Must be inside this scope.

classes.name: NotWithinScope
classes.doc: Must not be inside this scope.

classes.name: Cohort
classes.doc: These instances belong together. Prefer co-locating as components of ONE Actor where that applies — a landmark with two sockets is one Actor, unambiguous by construction. Reach for Cohort only when the members are genuinely separate placeables.

fields.name: all_or_nothing
fields.doc: Whether a partial placement is acceptable.

fields.name: ordered
fields.doc: Whether the order must be learnable.

classes.name: Preference
classes.doc: A soft placement bias. Relaxable, and REPORTED when relaxed — nothing is loose by accident.

classes.name: Exclusion
classes.doc: What forbids() returns: a volume nothing may occupy, with declared escapes.

classes.name: ScheduleRule
classes.doc: Ordering relative to other content.

fields.name: relaxable

classes.name: PlacedAfter
classes.doc: Place me after this target, with a gap.

classes.name: ExclusiveWith
classes.doc: Prefer not to appear alongside this.

classes.name: Supersedes
classes.doc: This replaces a base once available — the upgrade relationship.

classes.name: SpherePin
classes.doc: Pin to a sphere range. The first constraint about PACING rather than topology, and the one developers reach for soonest.

classes.name: Rationale
classes.doc: Why the core did what it did. The trace is built from these.

methods.name: subject
methods.doc: What this explains.

methods.name: layer
methods.doc: Which pipeline layer decided.

methods.name: inputs
methods.doc: What the decision read.

methods.name: explain
methods.doc: Prose.

methods.name: because
methods.doc: The upstream reasons, so a developer can walk back to the root cause.

classes.name: Context
classes.doc: The lens handed into every hook. Scope reads are FIELDS because they are free; queries are METHODS because they are not.

fields.name: reach
fields.doc: The enclosing Reach. The ONLY legal use of the reach stem — everywhere else the noun is range and the verb is accessible.

fields.name: space
fields.doc: The enclosing Space, which is what bounds geometry queries.

fields.name: floor
fields.doc: The enclosing Floor, which is what partitions accessibility.

fields.name: spatial
fields.doc: The content being considered at a position.

fields.name: slot
fields.doc: The spine slot in play, or null outside a spine. Read-only.

fields.name: held
fields.doc: Unlocks held. ROWS — one currency with grants() and HoldsRule. Already expanded through supersedes, so membership is a plain set test.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role assigned to the content under consideration.

fields.name: fidelity
fields.doc: How real the geometry currently is.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.doc: The bounded error of this fidelity rung. The ladder is monotone, so this only ever shrinks.

fields.name: rng
fields.doc: The ONLY randomness source. Anything else is unreplayable.

methods.name: state_of
methods.doc: Read a declared world-state variable.

methods.name: pool
methods.doc: Read a declared resource pool.

methods.name: setting
methods.doc: Read a project setting.

methods.name: query
methods.doc: The three-axis query builder: what to trace, what to consider, what to report. Declarative filters, never closures — a predicate callback survives neither the binding contract nor the palette.

methods.name: path_to
methods.doc: Realise a path to a target.

methods.name: accessible
methods.doc: Can an occupant holding these unlocks get from here to there? Trivalent, not bool, because the API must not be able to lie.

methods.name: within
methods.doc: Trivalent for METRIC questions. Dual bounds answer set membership; this answers 'is this ledge within 30 m', which every Span and Budget comparison actually asks.

methods.name: request
methods.doc: Ask the solver for something, softly.

methods.name: note
methods.doc: Add a reason to the trace.

methods.name: send_message
methods.doc: One-way notification to the host. Observational only, never affecting generation; debug_only messages are stripped entirely from a cooked build.

classes.name: ScopeHandle
classes.doc: A handle on one scope.

fields.name: floors
fields.doc: Floors inside this scope, if it is a Space.

methods.name: contains
methods.doc: Is this actor inside?

methods.name: accessible_from
methods.doc: Can an occupant holding these get here from there?

methods.name: instances_of
methods.doc: Placed content of a kind. Space and up — there is deliberately no floor-scoped instance query, because it would stop at a boundary the geometry does not stop at.

methods.name: dial
methods.doc: Read a numeric dial by its qualified <ClassName>.<DialName> id -- a scope handle may be any scope, so the owner is never implied. This is the DYNAMIC read; the typed one is the per-dial get node, which is picked and carries the dial's real type. Inherits OUTWARD-IN and an inner scope wins, so 'set saturation once at World scope' works. The trace records which scope supplied the value.

classes.name: Vec2
classes.doc: 2D vector. components, length, normalized, dot, distance_to, arithmetic, and the ZERO/ONE constants.

classes.name: Vec3
classes.doc: 3D vector. components, length, normalized, dot, cross, distance_to, arithmetic, and the ZERO/ONE/UP/DOWN/FORWARD/RIGHT constants.

classes.name: Quaternion
classes.doc: Rotation. from_euler, to_euler, slerp, mul.

classes.name: Mat4
classes.doc: 4x4 matrix. origin, basis, apply, inverse, mul.

classes.name: Transform
classes.doc: Position, rotation and scale. origin, basis, apply, inverse, mul.

classes.name: Aabb
classes.doc: Axis-aligned box. min, max, center, size, contains, intersects, expand, merge.

classes.name: Ray
classes.doc: Origin, direction, at(t).

classes.name: Plane
classes.doc: Normal, d, distance_to(p).

classes.name: Span
classes.doc: An inclusive range. min, max, contains, clamp, length, overlaps, lerp, is_bounded, and UNBOUNDED. A Span DECLARES a range; a Route OBLIGES one.

classes.name: Unlock
classes.doc: ONE ROW of an UnlockTableResource -- one atom of the progression lattice, something an occupant holds or knows. id, name, doc, supersedes. NOT A CLASS AND NOT A FILE: it carries no behaviour whatever, because every mechanical consequence belongs to a Component where affords/supports/judge can act on it. An unlock is an identity, and identity is all it is.

classes.name: Curve
classes.doc: 2D point data and NOT a resource — one row of a CurveTableResource. points, interpolation, sample, constant, ramp, from_points.

classes.name: Dial
classes.doc: A DEVELOPER-AUTHORED, named, tunable value owned by a Schematic or a Spine slot — how a host keeps fine-grained control over authored content at runtime. Identity is <ClassName>.<DialName>. Always exposed; always optional; the core ships none, and there is no such thing as a core dial. Holds a number, a hard range, a soft AdaptiveRange, an enum value, one curve, or a whole curve table whose named eval input it drives for every row. Resolves ONCE per generation pass, so it never changes underneath a decision mid-pass — which is why changing one is a different recipe and regenerates the world.

classes.name: AdaptiveRange
classes.doc: soft_min, hard_max, and target(available) computed from what is genuinely placeable. Falls below soft_min HONESTLY under content scarcity rather than padding with repeated filler or breaking outright.

classes.name: Quantity
classes.doc: initial, max, consumable.

classes.name: Pool
classes.doc: A resource an occupant draws on. capacity, reserve, and available(ctx) — the last is what every soft gate compares against, because capacity alone cannot answer how much is held at a given sphere.

classes.name: Harm
classes.doc: radius, severity 0..1, avoidable, continuous, mitigated_by, and NONE.

classes.name: Support
classes.doc: permitted (a Rule), max_slope, endurance (a Budget). Returned per occupant by Surface.supports.

classes.name: Approach
classes.doc: distance (a Span), max_slope, surface. What an occupant needs at the near end of a traversal.

classes.name: Occupant
classes.doc: Who is standing, as a parameter. actor (null for the player), is_player, held, holds(kind), footprint.

classes.name: Hit
classes.doc: A query result. valid, distance, point, normal, actor, component, island, polygon, triangle, surface, face, fidelity, and certainty. Fields below the achieved detail are ABSENT, which is checkable rather than sentinel-valued.

classes.name: DirectionCone
classes.doc: axis and angle. Replaces a three-value enum so that 'up, level or diagonally up, never down' is expressible.

classes.name: Kind
classes.doc: A picked CLASS path. path, is_a, and defaults() — the core-owned class default, one per class, READ and never built by content. This is how a token's authored values are compared without instantiating anything.

classes.name: Ref
classes.doc: A live INSTANCE reference. Never interchangeable with Kind: a class never appears in a value position and a path never in a type position.

classes.name: Tag
classes.doc: A dotted hierarchical label, picked rather than typed.

classes.name: TagQuery
classes.doc: A tag match with an exact/inherited toggle. Why an eligible-surface list survives every future surface being added.

classes.name: Cost
classes.doc: A kind and a limit, with NO accounting — Distance(m), Time(s) or Pool(pool, rate). What a Budget is a named instance of, and what an interaction spends.

classes.name: CollisionData
classes.doc: One collision island: a shape, placed, on a layer, meaning something. Collision is computed from the shape's PARAMETERS, never from tessellation — otherwise a visual LOD change silently alters generation.

fields.name: layer
fields.doc: Which broad phase it participates in. Hull is separate from Static so a conservative answer is never reported as a firm one.

fields.name: surface
fields.doc: What it MEANS to a mechanic — the resolved per-island answer queries hit.

classes.name: MetaValue
classes.doc: What a metadata value may hold. A CLOSED set, deliberately: an open Any would let content stash a handle the fingerprint cannot see, and the first symptom would be a world that fails to reproduce with no visible cause.

classes.name: BoolMeta
classes.doc: A yes or no.

classes.name: IntMeta
classes.doc: A whole number. i32, not i64: a JavaScript number is exact only below 2^53, and metadata crosses the binding seam constantly.

classes.name: FloatMeta
classes.doc: A real number.

classes.name: StringMeta
classes.doc: Text.

classes.name: Vec3Meta
classes.doc: A position or direction.

classes.name: TransformMeta
classes.doc: A placement.

classes.name: ArrayMeta
classes.doc: An ordered list of metadata values.

classes.name: MapMeta
classes.doc: A named map of metadata values.

classes.name: RefMeta
classes.doc: A reference to something with identity.

classes.name: BudgetRef
classes.doc: 'This budget' — Named(Ref<Budget>) into the project's book, or Inline(Cost) authored at the site. BOTH forms stay and stay DISTINGUISHABLE: forcing a one-off through the book is ceremony for a number used once, and because the two are told apart a tool can notice the same inline number in twelve places and offer to extract it.

classes.name: Quota
classes.doc: How many of something may exist, per scope.

classes.name: Diagnostic
classes.doc: An editor-time finding. Never blocks generation.

classes.name: Rng
classes.doc: The owned, forkable PRNG. Reached only through ctx.rng.

classes.name: Face
classes.doc: Which face of a bounding box something presents or mounts against.

values.name: POS_Y
values.doc: Up. The default mount face — a floor-standing thing.

values.name: NEG_Y
values.doc: Down. A ceiling mount.

classes.name: Role
classes.doc: What a placement turned out to be. An OUTPUT, assigned after the search from what it ran into — never declared.

values.name: DECORATION
values.doc: No mechanical consequence.

classes.name: ItemClass
classes.doc: What kind of reward something is. An INPUT the developer declares.

values.name: PROGRESSION
values.doc: May appear in logic. The conservative default.

values.name: USEFUL
values.doc: Tunes route difficulty, spends slack, never gates.

values.name: BONUS
values.doc: Rewards optional exploration. Auto-assigned to anything accessible solely through a relaxation.

values.name: FILLER
values.doc: Satisfies density. Currency, ammo, consumables.

classes.name: CollisionLayer
classes.doc: Which collision layer a body belongs to.

classes.name: QueryFilter
classes.doc: Coarse query scoping.

classes.name: Replenish
classes.doc: Whether and how a supply comes back.

classes.name: InstanceScope
classes.doc: How wide an instance query or effect reaches. There is deliberately NO FLOOR member: a floor-scoped instance query would stop at a boundary the geometry does not stop at.

classes.name: BooleanOp
classes.doc: Constructive solid geometry operations.

classes.name: ResolveState
classes.doc: How committed a node is. A subtree may lag but never lead.

values.name: PROJECTED
values.doc: A revisable forecast. The only state from which a node may be removed.

values.name: RESERVED
values.doc: Committed to exist, with an envelope claimed. Removable only by recorded backtracking.

values.name: REALIZED
values.doc: Built and frozen.

classes.name: Detail
classes.doc: How much a query wants back. Detail is what you ASK for; fidelity is what EXISTS.

values.name: SCOPE
values.doc: Which room. Available from L1.

values.name: COLLIDER
values.doc: Which box, which face. From L2.

values.name: INSTANCE
values.doc: Which placed actor, with its content path and metadata. From L2.

values.name: ISLAND
values.doc: Which mesh island. From L3.

values.name: POLYGON
values.doc: Which hull polygon or occupancy cell. From L3.

values.name: TRIANGLE
values.doc: Which triangle, with an interpolated normal. From L4.

classes.name: Fidelity
classes.doc: How real the geometry is. The ladder is monotone — each rung only tightens, so tolerance only shrinks.

values.name: ENVELOPE
values.doc: Tolerance is the envelope's own slack.

values.name: HULL
values.doc: Tolerance is the contouring tolerance.

values.name: GEOMETRY
values.doc: Tolerance is zero.

classes.name: Strictness
classes.doc: How hard a spine slot or preference must hold. Every relaxation is declared; nothing is loose by accident.

values.name: REQUIRED
values.doc: Must hold; if it cannot, generation fails with a diagnostic.

values.name: PREFERRED
values.doc: Strongly biased; may be relaxed when infeasible, and is REPORTED when it is.

values.name: OPTIONAL
values.doc: The generator decides freely; absence is expected.

classes.name: SkipPolicy
classes.doc: Per-lock sequence-break policy. A designer marks two or three gates, not two hundred.

values.name: TOLERATED
values.doc: A path exists; other emergent paths are fine. The default, because real games ship tolerated skips deliberately.

values.name: EXACT
values.doc: Report every alternative route found.

values.name: GUARDED
values.doc: Actively verify no alternative exists at that sphere, and fail loudly if one does. Also what decides whether a discovered shortcut may be adopted.

classes.name: Interpolation
classes.doc: How a curve row interpolates between keys. Declared PER ROW — UE fixes it per table only because a CSV has one header row, which JSON does not.

classes.name: Trivalent
classes.doc: Three-valued truth. A confident wrong answer is worse than an admitted unknown, so the API returns this rather than a bool wherever geometry is still approximate.

values.name: AMBIGUOUS
values.doc: Inside the ambiguous band. Resolve, never guess — and a decision that returns this re-asks at the next fidelity rung by construction.
